_about: Single authoritative release record; every page reads release facts from here. `current` names the release the site features; older releases stay in `releases` as version history. A release is public only when `status` is "released" AND the owner has approved it: then `date`, `sha256` and its `method`'s fields must all be set (the build refuses anything else). `method`: `discord` = the official release post on the Project Blonde Discord (`download.url` is that post's permanent link, never a signed attachment URL); `patcher` = made in the visitor's browser from content/patcher.json. `public_version` must equal blonde/release/public-version.json and the title screen. v1.1 facts are copied from output/project-blonde-v1.1-rc-v111-20261010/release-information.json. No URL, date, checksum or patch detail is invented here.

releases.save_compatibility: No save-format change. Two saves written by public v1.0 were continued in v1.1, saved in the game and loaded again after a cold restart; location, party, inventory, money, coins, Badges and story progress matched. Tested with the mGBA 0.10.5 engine; not tested on Delta or on physical hardware.
releases.save_compatibility_short: Saves from v1.0 continue with an ordinary Continue. Back up first.
highlights: Johto, Kanto and Hoenn in one adventure, on one save file.
482 Pokémon to find, including 42 regional forms.
Mega Evolution, the DexNav and Pokémon that follow you.

changelog: Refreshed trainer and NPC appearances with custom Gen 3-style sprites: 273 overworld assignments, 49 dialogue portrait assignments and 10 Lass battle assignments.
Improved consistency between overworld characters, dialogue portraits and battle artwork.
Updated Lass and Firebreather battle artwork.
Refreshed Alola palm trees and improved Alola DexNav grass animation with a pulsing glint.
The approved animated Gold and Wigglytuff title screen now displays v1.1 beneath PRESS START.
known_limitations: Some NPC graphics remain cached when loading an older save. Leave and re-enter the map to refresh them.
Martin on Route 12 and Jake/Joyce on Route 26 retain inherited off-map placements. Their assigned graphics are present, but these three actors have not been observed live.
Testing used headless mGBA 0.10.5 and disposable save copies. Delta/iOS, physical hardware and a complete story playthrough were not tested for this release candidate.
All phone/rematch schedules, every weather/reflection/resource-pressure combination and every Alola search outcome have not been exhaustively tested.
Title music data and active playback state match v110. Audio was not listened to or captured during these tests.

instructions: Back up the old game and its normal in-game save.
Use the Delta import/export guide or matching mGBA filenames and save path.
Cold launch and choose CONTINUE; do not transfer an old save state.
Leave/re-enter the map to refresh cached NPC graphics.
Verify party, bag, badges, money and location, then save and back up again.
facts: Use Continue from a cold launch. Do not carry an emulator save state across this update. If you only have a save state, load it in the old version and make a normal in-game save first.
Some NPC graphics can stay cached until you leave and re-enter the map.

The game file is still named Pokemon - Project Blonde.gba. A normal mGBA save uses the matching name Pokemon - Project Blonde.sav. If your files use another name, keep that matching pair on copies; do not rename or overwrite your only backup.
If Continue is missing, stop and check the imported save or the save path before starting a new game.
To go back, restore the old game with its own pre-update save backup. Do not rely on a newer save or a save state for downgrading.

guides.name: iPhone & iPad
steps: In the old game, use the game’s SAVE command. Return to Delta’s library.
Long-press the old game: Manage Save File → Export Save File. Save a dated backup in Files. Keep the old game and this backup.
Download the ZIP from the official Discord downloads post. Extract it in Files. In Delta, tap + and import the extracted Pokemon - Project Blonde.gba.
Long-press the updated game: Manage Save File → Import Save File. Select a copy of your exported normal save. The changed game may appear as a separate library entry.
Cold-launch the updated game, check the v1.1 label, then choose Continue. Check party, bag, Badges, money and location. Leave and re-enter the map if old NPC artwork is still visible.
Save inside the game and export a fresh backup. Keep the pre-update backup too.
guides.note: Use the normal save, not an old emulator save state. If Continue is missing, check the save import before starting New Game. This procedure was written from Delta’s official controls; v1.1 was not tested on an iPhone or iPad.

guides.name: Windows & macOS
steps: Save inside the old game, then close mGBA. Copy the old .gba and normal .sav into a dated backup folder. Keep that backup unchanged.
Check mGBA Settings → Paths for your Save games location. By default, saves are beside the game file; a custom path overrides this.
Download and extract the official Discord ZIP into a new folder. Keep the filename Pokemon - Project Blonde.gba.

Copy your backed-up normal save into the configured save location with the matching name Pokemon - Project Blonde.sav. If that path already has a save, back it up before replacing it. If you use a custom save path, make sure the backup is outside that active path.

Open the extracted .gba in mGBA, confirm v1.1 on the title, then select Continue. Do not load an old save state. Check party, bag, Badges, money and location; leave and re-enter the map to refresh cached NPC graphics.
Save inside the game, close mGBA, reopen and confirm Continue loads your progress. Keep both the old backup and a fresh v1.1 save backup.
guides.note: If your old game file uses a personal name, keep a matching .gba / .sav pair on copies. If Continue is missing, recheck filenames and Settings → Paths before starting New Game. Save migration was tested with the mGBA 0.10.5 engine; the mGBA application window itself was not automated.

A typo in his call after the sixteenth Badge. Fixed in v103.
Your Hoenn rival called it an Itemfinder on Route 110. Fixed in v103.
Seven Leaders described level caps and HM permissions that do not apply in Project Blonde. Rewritten in v104.
